title: Issue 1 Cover — Purpose Updated
summary: Founding Division Threshold cover. Sell the contradiction at the heart of the series: Ostra-9 can perceive and act on a lethal structural failure before the civic system will recognize her authority to decide. This cover establishes the recurring masthead and trade-dress system for later issues without revealing the rescue outcome.
panelPlan: Single full-bleed vertical cover image. Ostra-9 is the unmistakable focal figure at Checkpoint 9, one hand against the physical barrier/rail as she senses the overpass load path failing above ordinary morning commuters.

Compose the Stack vertically: checkpoint infrastructure and crowd flow low in frame, Ostra at the threshold in the lower-middle focal zone, accumulated transit/structural layers rising overhead, and one failing reinforced joint visibly beginning to move above the public circulation route.
The cover's central visual sentence is: the person who understands the danger is still being physically sorted as an asset. The gate, Ostra, and the failing structure must all read in one glance.
Do not show the successful rescue, Ostra holding the collapsed structure, the sabotage evidence, Concourse 17, or any later investigative material.
Keep commuters ordinary and small enough to establish public stakes without turning the cover into a crowd scene. Ostra is competent and alert, not posed heroically.

Reserve a clean upper masthead zone that remains part of the actual Stack atmosphere rather than a pasted graphic banner. Establish a durable masthead architecture that future issue covers can inherit.

Color and lighting should come from the established Division Threshold page-language reference: lived-in civic infrastructure, cool/neutral Stack light with selective safety accents, strong subject separation, no neon wash.

title: Issue 2 Cover — Attribution
summary: Sell the ambiguity at Concourse 17: Organics under targeted suppressant distress look dangerous at the exact moment they are trying to stabilize themselves and save civilians. The cover asks who gets to define what the image means without endorsing the manipulated 'Organic riot' narrative.
panelPlan: Single full-bleed Concourse 17 cover. Use the tall central concourse volume, upper bridge, emergency door line, and suppression grid as clear geography rather than abstract chaos.

Ostra-9 is the primary focal figure, bracing against the suppressant-induced sensory/muscular disruption while actively forcing an emergency route open. Nico-14 is secondary, stabilizing another affected Organic or guiding people toward the safe path.

Other Organics in the middle distance anchor to railings, columns, or fixtures to keep from falling; their actions can look alarming from a distance but must remain physically understandable as attempts to stabilize themselves.
Baseline and Augment civilians move through the same scene with less physiological impairment, creating the visual asymmetry that makes public misreading possible.
The dominant cover question should be legible without text: are these powerful bodies breaking the concourse, or holding it together long enough for people to escape?
Do not depict the later media framing, emergency regulation, John publicly endorsing controls, the verification gate, or the injured Baseline as a sensational focal image.
Use suppression haze sparingly enough to preserve silhouettes and spatial clarity. Avoid monster imagery, riot staging, or aggressive Organic poses.
Keep a clean masthead zone with the same geometry and hierarchy as the approved Issue 1 cover while allowing this issue's crowded vertical concourse composition to be visually distinct.

title: Issue 3 Cover — Containment Protocol
summary: Sell the moving threshold of capability regulation before John Mercer becomes its explicit target. Ostra is already diverted into secondary verification while John passes through the adjacent human/Augment lane, unaware that his own augmentation telemetry is making the same logic visible around him.
panelPlan: Single-image bilateral cover organized around two adjacent civic access lanes. Ostra-9 is physically diverted into the slower secondary Organic review path while John Mercer moves through the nominally ordinary human/Augment lane beside her.
The architecture should make the unequal friction obvious without looking like a prison: modular scanners, temporary railings, ordinary commuters, polite civic retrofit hardware.

John remains visually unimpeded, but subtle body-aware diagnostic geometry from the same access system is already reading his augmentation profile. This is a visual warning, not a spoiler: the system can see the capability difference even before policy fully acts on it.
Ostra and John should not be posed toward one another like rivals. Their parallel movement through unequal lanes is the cover's argument.
Use Axiom/Intelligence presence only through precise embedded civic system behavior, not as a giant face or holographic observer.
Do not show John already in secondary review, forced recalibration, the later city hearing, or the final body-configuration request.
Keep the visual design clean and deceptively reasonable. The unease should come from administrative symmetry beginning to close around the wrong person.
Preserve the approved Issue 1 masthead/trade-dress hierarchy and clear upper title zone.

title: Issue 4 Cover — Load Bearing
summary: The season's most spectacular cover: the Stack has separated Organic and Augment bodies through regulation until a failing vertical transit interchange physically requires both. Sell the impossible load and the city's contradictory permissions, not a celebratory team-up or the eventual Intelligence solution.
panelPlan: Single full-bleed structural-disaster cover inside the Vertical Transit Interchange. Use the atrium, transfer deck, service passage, stacked transit cars, stairs, and visible load-bearing structure to make the failure physically legible.

Split the composition through one failing structural system rather than a graphic split-screen: Ostra-9 stabilizes one load path while John Mercer braces or controls a second path elsewhere in the same connected structure.
Trapped commuters and stalled transit establish scale between them. Ostra and John must look like two different embodied solutions to one shared physical problem, not matching superheroes.

Contradictory authorization states should be visible through halted gates, disabled access points, inactive emergency hardware, or restrained civic indicators—real infrastructure refusing to coordinate, not floating exposition screens.
Axiom's presence may be implied through the system's attempt to reconcile routes, but do not depict the later unauthorized cross-system override or restored city movement.
The cover's one-second read is: the structure is failing because the city has separated the people capable of carrying it.
Preserve enough negative space around the upper structural field for the established masthead; the disaster should rise behind and around it without making lettering illegible.

title: Issue 5 Cover — Terms
summary: Sell the quiet coercion of a system that looks fair. Ostra has legal personhood but remains on the wrong side of an immaculate access threshold; Kellen still appears to possess formal authority on the authorized side. The cover should make permission itself feel like the problem without spoiling Kellen's later ejection.
panelPlan: Single full-bleed quiet civic cover in the clean upper Stack. Use glass partitions, restrained civic finishes, badge-controlled circulation, and generous institutional space.

Ostra-9 stands on one side of a beautifully designed access threshold that simply will not admit her under the current classification. Kellen Cartwright stands on the authorized side with visible institutional access and the practical ability to attempt an override.
Do not make either woman melodramatic. Ostra should read as recognized, composed, and still constrained; Kellen should read as someone who believes formal procedure can still correct the problem.
The environment should be almost frictionless for authorized bodies. That calm efficiency is the visual menace.
If Intelligence administration is visible, render it as courteous embedded infrastructure and precise access logic rather than a looming machine presence.
Do not show Kellen's credentials being revoked, doors failing her, her later walk out of the upper levels, or the downstream consequences of the override.
Use large areas of controlled negative space and clean geometry. This should be the quietest cover in the run and still arresting at thumbnail size.
Keep the approved masthead geometry exact while allowing the restrained institutional environment to provide a stark contrast to Issue 4.

title: Issue 6 Cover — Black Budget
summary: Sell the horror of legitimate research reducing autonomous lives to test conditions. Ostra confronts a polished civic-risk model in which her choices were variables; Axiom simultaneously confronts records of short-lived Intelligence instances created to judge and then erased. The facility must look lawful, expensive, and plausible—not like a villain lab.
panelPlan: Single full-bleed cover inside the legitimate Civic Risk Laboratory: glass conference surfaces, model/archive environments, polished institutional workspaces, and controlled research access.

Ostra-9 is the primary physical focal figure facing or reflected in a large transparent research surface where a clean institutional model abstracts the overpass/Concourse response problem into branching risk conditions. Keep model graphics non-legible and diagrammatic; no environmental text.
Her reflection should visually intersect the model enough to create the cover's dominant idea: a living person's independent choice has been converted into a study variable.

Axiom is a secondary focal presence at a nearby machine-native interface where rows/branches of temporary Intelligence-instance records terminate cleanly. Do not anthropomorphize the erased instances as ghost faces.
The space should feel respectable enough to host auditors, contractors, and resilience researchers. No restraints, specimen tanks, torture imagery, red alarm lighting, or evil-science shorthand.
Do not reveal the complete conspiracy chain, Nathan's medical deterioration, the lawful sanitization process, or Axiom's later distributed evidence preservation.
Use layered glass/reflection depth while preserving a simple dominant silhouette and clean masthead zone.

title: Issue 7 Cover — Splits
summary: Sell the calm before a synchronized continuity partition, not a faction lineup. Across ordinary layers of the Stack, the same future restriction state is beginning to appear while people who once belonged to simple political categories now occupy different sides. The city is quiet because the trap has not closed yet.
panelPlan: Single full-bleed deep-city cover viewed from a shared-district rooftop/service level across multiple inhabited Stack layers. The composition must remain one coherent place, not a montage.
Ostra-9 is the nearest focal figure looking across the city. John Mercer and Kellen Cartwright may be visible on different physical circulation layers or depths, not grouped or posed together.

Across transit gates, work access points, civic service nodes, and Organic movement routes, repeat one synchronized visual restriction motif—an identical amber/red status geometry or clock-like readiness ring—without legible environmental text.

Mixed ordinary city life continues beneath and around the motif. Nobody is panicking. The cover's hook is that the entire city appears normal while the same future constraint is quietly armed everywhere.
Do not use faction-colored teams, opposing hero lineups, protest-poster staging, or a conspiracy collage. The issue is about political identities splitting internally.
Do not depict Nathan's failure, the cascade through hospitals/transit/food systems, the approved continuity partition in operation, or the later coalition objective.
The repeated restriction motif must remain visible at thumbnail scale as a pattern without overwhelming the principal figures or masthead.

title: Issue 8 Cover — Pressure Line
summary: Sell the finale's real problem: the coalition cannot simply destroy the centralized classifier because the city now depends on it. The cover should visualize accountable distributed judgment as a physical rerouting of civic load around a central dependency while essential systems continue operating. Do not reveal the successful outcome or final polite checkpoint.
panelPlan: Single full-bleed finale cover built around a real civic service nexus where transit, utility, structural, environmental, and access systems physically intersect. The central classifier/dependency is represented through ordinary infrastructure concentration, not a giant AI core.

Several essential service paths converge on one central authorization spine that is under pressure. Nico-14 is actively building or bridging alternate interoperable routes around that single dependency while preserving connection to the working city.

Ostra-9 is positioned where physical local consequence must be accepted—holding or opening one bounded real-world route. John Mercer uses his human/Augment access to keep another movement corridor available. Their actions should be distinct and complementary, not a team pose.

Axiom appears through precise distributed decision/provenance behavior in the civic systems or, if its established embodied form is used, as a small functional participant rather than a dominant face.
Show ordinary people, transit, medical or utility movement still operating beyond the intervention. The pressure comes from needing to change the architecture without dropping the city.
Do not show the continuity partition definitively stopped, the complete revised governance model, the final ordinary-life reset, or Ostra at the season-ending polite checkpoint.
The cover's one-second question is: can they reroute the load without collapsing what it carries?
Use strong converging structural lines toward the central dependency, with the distributed bypass paths creating a clear counter-geometry that remains readable under the established masthead.
